e.etymology: A respelling of Harlem, the Manhattan neighborhood that Dutch settlers named in 1658 after the city of Haarlem in the Netherlands.
In Norway and Sweden, from juni, the month of June, partly as a translation of the English name June. In the US it also serves as a pet form of Juniper, June or Junia.
namesakes: Juni Cortez (the younger brother in the Spy Kids films)

assoc.t: Juni Cortez of the Spy Kids films

e.etymology: From Slavic mir, peace, with the common name suffix -an; a familiar name in Slovenia and Croatia. The same spelling is also a Kurdish and Turkish boys' name.
Created by American author Sarah J. Maas for Aelin Galathynius, the heroine of her Throne of Glass fantasy novels, which began in 2012.
namesakes: Aelin Galathynius (heroine of Sarah J. Maas's Throne of Glass novels)

assoc.t: Aelin Galathynius, heroine of the Throne of Glass novels

e.etymology: A German short form of names beginning with irm- or erm-, whole or entire, such as Irmgard. It reached English in the 1800s and is a cousin of Emma.
namesakes: Irma Rombauer (author of The Joy of Cooking)
Irma Thomas (singer known as the Soul Queen of New Orleans)

assoc.t: Hurricane Irma, which struck Florida in 2017

e.etymology: A respelling of Jason, from Greek Iason, linked to iasthai, to heal. In Greek myth Jason led the Argonauts in the quest for the Golden Fleece.
A modern American coinage in the style of Aniyah and Taniyah, joining a Ka- opening to the -iyah ending.
A respelling of Kenley, an English place name and surname from Old English, Cena's clearing. It came into use for girls in the 2000s alongside Kinley and Kenzie.
A feminine spelling of Teddy, the pet form of Theodora and Theodore, from Greek theos, god, and doron, gift. Teddy has also long served as a pet form of Edward.
namesakes: Teddi Mellencamp (Real Housewives of Beverly Hills cast member)

assoc.t: teddy bear, the stuffed toy (same sound)

e.etymology: A spelling of Samira, the feminine of Samir, from Arabic samara, to pass the evening in conversation: a companion for talk after dark.
From Arabic zayn, beauty, and zina, adornment. Zeina is the spelling favored in Lebanon and Egypt.
A spelling of Rory, the English form of Irish Ruairí and Scottish Gaelic Ruairidh, from Old Irish Ruaidrí, red king.
A spelling of Raya, a name found in several unrelated languages. Raya drew attention in the US with Disney's 2021 film Raya and the Last Dragon.
From Arabic rahma, mercy, by way of Persian and Urdu rahmat. In Punjabi it is given by Sikh and Muslim families alike, with the sense of God's grace.

e.meaning: pet form of Joseph (he will add) or Judith (woman of Judea)
e.etymology: For girls, a variant of Judy, the pet form of Judith; for boys, a pet form of Joseph. The boy hero of the 1938 novel The Yearling spread the male use.
namesakes: Jody Baxter (the boy in The Yearling)

assoc.t: military slang for a man who steals a soldier's partner

e.note: In US military slang, a Jody is the man back home who takes up with a deployed soldier's partner.

e.etymology: From French alizé, the steady trade wind of the tropics. In the US the name rose in the 1990s along with Alizé, a French liqueur that was a fixture of hip-hop lyrics.

assoc.t: Alizé, French cognac and passion fruit liqueur

e.note: Shares its name with Alizé, a cognac-based liqueur well known from 1990s hip-hop.

e.etymology: A respelling of Caden, which rose in the early 2000s on the popularity of similar-sounding names such as Aidan, Braden, Hayden and Jadon.
A pet form of David, from Hebrew dawid, beloved. Long a Scottish boys' nickname, it is now given in the US mostly to girls, in the manner of Stevie and Billie.
From Arabic sahil, shore or coast, borrowed into Persian, Urdu and Hindi. It is a familiar boys' name across India and Pakistan.
The Arabic elative of karim, generous or noble, so it means most generous. The Quran uses al-Akram, the Most Bountiful, as a description of God.
From Quechua amaru, the great serpent of Andean myth. It was borne by the Inca ruler Tupac Amaru and by rapper Tupac Amaru Shakur, named after the rebel leader Tupac Amaru II.
namesakes: Tupac Amaru Shakur (rapper, who carried it as his middle name)

e.etymology: A modern American coinage, a compact spelling in the family of Zaire and Zyaire.
A modern name with no single source. For boys it follows Lian and Liam and is used largely by Spanish-speaking families; for girls it can be a spelling of the Arabic name Layan.
In India, from Sanskrit vira, brave or heroic, the root of Veer. In Finland and Estonia, Veera is the local form of Russian Vera, faith.

e.meaning: dweller by the row of houses or hedgerow
e.etymology: An English surname, in most families for someone who lived by a row of houses or a hedgerow, in others a medieval form of Rolf or Ralph. Its use as a first name is recent.
A merging of Anne and Marie, modeled on French Anne-Marie and long used in Germany, the Netherlands and Denmark. Anne goes back to Hebrew Hannah, grace, and Marie to Mary.
namesakes: Annemarie Johansen (heroine of Lois Lowry's novel Number the Stars)

e.etymology: From Yiddish gold, gold, a traditional name among Ashkenazi Jews. Golda Meir, Israel's prime minister from 1969 to 1974, is its best-known bearer.
namesakes: Golda Meir (prime minister of Israel, 1969 to 1974)

assoc.t: Golda Meir, Israel's prime minister from 1969 to 1974

e.etymology: A Y- spelling of Julissa, an elaboration of Julia that took hold among Spanish-speaking families in the 1990s. Julia comes from the Roman family name Julius.
A respelling of Christian, from Latin Christianus, follower of Christ, built on Greek Khristos, the anointed one. Christian has been an English given name since the twelfth century.
From Arabic farhan, happy or joyful, from farah, joy. It is widely used across South Asia, especially in Bangladesh, Pakistan and India.
A respelling of Kensley, an American name of the 2010s shaped by Kinsley and Kenzie, here with the popular -lee ending.
The month name used as a given name. October comes from Latin octo, eight, because it was the eighth month of the early Roman calendar.
